subject: health
title: Healthy Habits
about: Germs and handwashing, coughing into the elbow, staying home when sick, baby teeth and brushing, enough sleep, and dressing for the weather. NC 1.PCH.1 (behaviors that promote health); handwashing comes up in cold season and dental health in February.
tip: Sing the ABC song together while he scrubs his hands tonight; that is about 20 seconds.

cards.q: Tiny living things that can make you sick are called what?
cards.note: Germs are so small you need a microscope to see them.

cards.q: Can you see germs with your eyes?
cards.note: Germs can be on your hands even when your hands look clean.

cards.q: How do germs move from one person to another?
cards.note: Germs ride on tiny drops from a cough or a sneeze, and on hands.

cards.q: What is the best way to get germs off your hands?
cards.note: Soap lifts the germs off and the water washes them away.

cards.q: How long do you scrub your hands with soap?
cards.note: Sing the ABC song while you scrub.

cards.q: When should you wash your hands?
cards.note: Wash before you eat and after you use the bathroom.

cards.q: Where do you cough or sneeze?
cards.note: Your elbow does not touch doors, toys or friends, so germs stay put.

cards.q: You have a fever. Where should you stay?
cards.note: Resting at home helps you get better and keeps germs away from friends.

cards.q: Your first set of teeth are called what?
cards.note: Baby teeth start to fall out around age six.

cards.q: A baby tooth falls out. What grows in its place?
cards.note: Grown-up teeth are also called permanent teeth.

cards.q: How many baby teeth do most kids have?
cards.note: Count them in rows of five.

cards.q: How many times a day do you brush your teeth?
cards.note: Brush in the morning and before bed, for two minutes each time.
The dentist counts your teeth and cleans them.

cards.q: Your tooth hurts. What do you do?
cards.note: A grown-up can take you to the dentist to make it better.

cards.q: How many hours of sleep does a first grader need?
cards.note: Doctors say kids 6 to 12 need 9 to 12 hours each night.

cards.q: It is snowing. What do you wear?
cards.note: Warm clothes keep your body heat in on a cold day.

cards.q: It is raining. What keeps you dry?
cards.note: Rain boots keep your feet dry too.

cards.q: It is hot and sunny. What do you wear?
cards.note: Sunscreen and a hat protect your skin from the sun.
